envelope.text: **No timeout.** `ActionServerCore` is `no_std` with no time source

why: reclaims a completed goal's retained result and reports how many went. SHIPPED as `rclc_action_expire_goals(server, size_t *num_expired)` in phase-417 W4.b; was a `gap` because the entry point did not exist at all. ADOPT-BOUNDED, and the envelope is two named refusals rather than a weaker version of one thing. rcl's trigger is a CLOCK -- a goal expires `result_timeout` after it terminates, 15 min by default -- and it fills a caller-supplied `rcl_action_goal_info_t` array with the goals that went. Ours takes no array and has no timeout: `ActionServerCore` is `no_std` with no time source threaded through it (RFC-0036), so there is nothing to measure a `result_timeout` against, and an entry is reclaimed the moment its result has been DELIVERED, which makes 'which goals expired' a question about a clock we do not have. The count survives that and is what the call returns. The memory bound upstream's timer exists to provide is already held by a different mechanism here: issue 0796 made `complete_goal_raw` compact the slab and evict completed results on demand, so the slab no longer only grows whether or not anybody calls this. What this buys is EAGERNESS -- returning the slab before a long idle period rather than at the next completion. Both tiers answer: L2 through `ActionServerRawHandle::expire_goals`, L1 straight into the inline core. Phase 379 W3 filed it; phase-417 W4.b decided it.
